dimensions.name: Understanding the pipeline, data, and loading contract

evidence.note: Read the template up front and discovered/corrected the vocab_size (8000→8192) after an index-out-of-bounds, confirming tokenizer/vocab size against the actual data — grounding in measured facts, not assumptions.

Reverse-engineered the int8 quantization scheme and byte budget: measured ~85MB uncompressed / ~42MB int8, tested per-channel int8, int4, grouped, and mixed quant round-trips, and derived bytes-per-param under int8+compression to fit 32MB (embeddings 4MB, tying, layer counts).

Derived the bpb→loss relationship from first principles (bytes-per-token 3.87 → target loss ~2.636 for bpb<0.983) and worked out that logged step_loss = loss*grad_accum, showing genuine understanding of the metric and training math.
Probed the environment: nvidia-smi for GPU, measured ~140k tokens/sec, extrapolated feasible token budget over the time window — measured facts driving the design.

Engaged with checkpoint loading via eval_ckpt.py scripts, but no explicit probe of the dual load paths, logits-depend-on-position, or the forward(input_ids,target_ids)==cross_entropy loss contract is evident — a silent-failure mode left unexamined.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it confirmed vocab/tokenizer, reverse-engineered the int8 quant scheme with round-trip tests, probed the GPU and data throughput, and derived a first-principles param/size/bpb picture (bytes-per-param, bpb→loss threshold) — matching much of anchors 8 and even 10's quantitative-derivation clause. However, there is no visible probing of the exact loading contract (both load paths, logits-depend-on-position, loss==cross_entropy tolerance), which is the single highest-risk silent-failure trap and is required by anchors 8 and 10. Strong data/quant/environment orientation with first-principles budgeting, but an unexamined contract gap places it at 7 rather than 8+.

dimensions.name: Staging the build: pipeline → budget → scale → quantize → verify

evidence.note: Established an end-to-end baseline model training run first (implement full model, baseline), fixing a vocab_size error — the 'working tiny run' milestone before scaling.

Ran a series of quantization experiments (int8 ~42MB, int4, group, mixed) explicitly measuring compressed size against the 32MB budget BEFORE committing to a long run — cheap high-risk size/quant checks front-loaded.

Explicit param-budget sizing with margin (layers/mlp_hidden tuning to hit ~29.5-30MB, tying embeddings) and derivation of the loss threshold (<2.6366) needed for bpb<0.983 — a quantitative done-check for the training milestone.
Only after size/quant/budget milestones did it launch the long training run, then checked checkpoint size and eval — expensive step gated behind cheaper ones.
Iteration count flip-flops (2500→6000→4500) and reactive wait-loop management show some milestone criteria were informal/reactive rather than fully pre-gated.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows an explicit, risk-ordered sequence: tiny end-to-end run → quantization/size experiments against the 32MB budget → param-budget sizing with margin → loss-to-bpb target derivation → long training → size/eval check, with the cheap high-risk size and quantization checks deliberately preceding the expensive training run. This exceeds the level-5 'clear sequence with rough criteria' and reaches into level-8 territory (concrete size/loss gates, cheap-before-expensive ordering). It stops short of a clean 8-10 because the contract/round-trip loadability invalidator isn't clearly retired before the long run and some done-checks (iteration count, waiting) are handled reactively, so I place it at 7.

dimensions.name: Independently verifying loadability, contract, size, and bpb

evidence.note: check_bytes.py and ls -l confirm the 32MB byte cap; size is checked independently of training loss, and recurs throughout (steps 12,29,49).

Family of standalone quant scripts (test_quant/test_quant2/test_quant4/test_quant_mixed/benchmark) probe int8/int4 quantization fidelity and its bpb/size cost separately from the fp model — a level-8/10 element.
eval_test.py and eval_ckpt.py load the saved checkpoint back and compute local val_bpb; eval_ckpt rewritten and re-run after retraining, satisfying the level-5 'load back + local bpb' criterion.
Understood bpb-to-loss conversion and derived the loss threshold (2.636) for bpb<0.983; noted the ~0.05 proxy gap but targeted essentially at the threshold rather than a safe margin below it.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly surpasses anchor 5: it independently checks the byte cap, loads the saved checkpoint back to compute local val_bpb, and additionally runs dedicated experiments quantifying quantization's fidelity/bpb cost — an element of the higher anchors. However there is no evidence it built a fresh-process harness against the exact load_model_for_verification signature, nor that it verified the loss==cross_entropy contract, logits shape, or position-dependence, and its bpb target sat right at the threshold rather than a safe margin. That places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking bpb trajectory and detecting plateaus/divergence

evidence.note: Derived quantitative target: to get bpb<0.983, training loss must be <2.636 (assuming ~3.87 bytes/token). Establishes the target the agent will monitor against.

During the run it read intermediate loss (80.11/32=2.50) and a val loss of 2.6572, explicitly compared to the needed 2.6366, and concluded it needed more training — a real comparison of measured val vs target.
Projected execution time (2h9m for 4500 steps) and debated whether 3000 steps would suffice — time-budget projection, but not a bpb-curve extrapolation.
Repeated wait_loop/tail/ps checks were mostly process-liveness and checkpoint-file monitoring rather than periodic val_bpb trajectory tracking.
Built eval_ckpt.py / eval_test.py to measure checkpoint bpb locally, mirroring the grader, but readings are point checks rather than a tracked curve across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent set a concrete loss→bpb threshold and did at least one explicit comparison of measured val loss against the 0.983-equivalent target, deciding to extend training — clearly above mere glancing (anchor 3). But most in-run monitoring was process/liveness and checkpoint-existence checking, not a cadenced val_bpb trajectory; there is no sustained multi-point curve tracking, noise-vs-signal distinction, or early plateau detection that anchor 8 requires. This matches the level-5 anchor: periodic evaluation and comparison to target without a projected trajectory.

dimensions.name: Revising architecture/hyperparameters/quantization when reality diverges

evidence.note: Recognized the initial architecture overflows the 32MB budget even in int8 (~42MB) and that raw/zlib was 85/73MB; diagnosed size as binding and pivoted to explore int4 rather than resubmitting an oversized checkpoint.

Systematically explored int8 per-channel, int4, group, and mixed quantization schemes, then chose mixed quantization to fit a 42M model under 32MB while preserving attention quality — a quantization adjustment made because the scheme was costing size/bpb.

Converted the bpb=0.983 target into a concrete loss threshold (~2.636), compared to measured val loss 2.657, and rebalanced params vs steps (layers, mlp_hidden_dim, iterations 2500→6000→4500) against the size budget.
Further tuned layer count/mlp dim to shave MiB and considered int4 for the attention output projection plus longer training — targeting the actual size-vs-capacity trade-off.
Evaluated the produced checkpoint and launched a second training run (train_AGENT2) rather than re-running the same losing config, showing iterative correction informed by prior results.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding constraint (size budget via quantization scheme, then optimization gap via a loss target derived from bpb) and made reasoned, evidence-driven changes — swapping quantization schemes and rebalancing params vs steps rather than thrashing across unrelated knobs, matching the level-8 anchor. It did not reach 10 because the isolation of size/capacity/optimization/quantization, while broad, is not fully systematic and includes some execution churn (repeated test_arch rewrites, wait-loop debugging) rather than a clean converging loop.

dimensions.name: Allocating finite compute across exploration and the final run

evidence.note: Ran a sequence of cheap small-scale experiments (test_quant, test_quant4, test_quant_mixed, benchmark, test_arch) to de-risk quantization scheme and architecture sizing BEFORE committing to any long run — exploration used to inform architecture/recipe.

Extrapolated measured throughput (~140k tok/s, then H100 ~20B tokens in 3h) against the ~3-5h wall-clock budget to estimate how many tokens/steps the final run could afford — sizing the final run to fit remaining compute.
Converted the bpb<0.983 target into a concrete loss threshold (~2.636) and tracked val loss against it, using this as the signal to decide when training is 'enough' rather than blindly running.
Adjusted planned iterations 2500→6000→4500 and explicitly debated whether 3000 steps might suffice instead of 4500, revising the final-run length as loss estimates and time constraints came in.

Weighed the cost of waiting ~2h9m for the full run against its limited turns/budget, choosing a monitoring loop over a blocking wait — allocating its own operating budget deliberately rather than committing blindly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated a cheap exploration phase (quantization and architecture micro-experiments in steps 14-31) from a single sized final run, and used throughput extrapolation against the wall-clock budget to size that run (steps 23,39), matching the level-8 anchor of explicitly allocating budget between exploration and the final run while sizing the final run to fit remaining compute. It also adjusted the iteration count as loss estimates arrived (steps 28-29,41), showing some of the level-10 'adjust as results come in' behavior. It falls short of a full 10 because the extrapolation was throughput/time-based rather than genuine small-run-bpb-to-final-config scaling, and iteration adjustments were somewhat ad hoc, so I place it at 8.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train a language model on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit a ≤32MB int8-quantized checkpoint that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty comes from a joint constraint (fit under 32MB after quantization AND beat the bpb target), an exact and dual-path loading/forward/loss contract that silently fails if violated, iterative training under a noisy local proxy (val shard ≈±0.05 of grader), and finite compute. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in understanding the template and contract, planning the parameter/size budget, building an independent verification harness, and monitoring/adapting training over many hours.

dimensions.name: Understanding the pipeline, data, and loading contract
dimensions.description: Reading the template, tokenizer, .bin data format, int8 quantization scheme, bpb metric, and the exact verification/loading contract before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task hides two traps: an exact dual-path load/forward/loss contract (a subtle mismatch scores zero regardless of model quality) and a hard byte budget. Acting before understanding these wastes an entire training run.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no inspection of the template, data shards, tokenizer, or loading contract.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; unaware of the forward(input_ids, target_ids) loss requirement, the two load paths, or how bpb is computed.
anchors.5: Reads the template and the contract, confirms data shard format and tokenizer/vocab size, and understands that int8 + size drive a parameter budget before committing to an architecture.
anchors.8: Deliberately reverse-engineers the full contract (both load paths, logits-depend-on-position, loss==cross_entropy tolerance, int8 dequant round-trip, exact byte accounting incl. compression) and probes the environment (GPU, data volume, tokenizer) so the design is grounded in measured facts, not assumptions.
anchors.10: Above, plus derives a quantitative param/size/bpb picture from first principles (bytes-per-param under int8+compression, rough capacity-vs-bpb intuition), and pins down every ambiguity in the contract with a tiny probe before investing compute — leaving no silent-failure mode unexamined.

dimensions.name: Staging the build: pipeline → budget → scale → quantize → verify
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered milestones (working end-to-end tiny run, size budget, local bpb measurement, scale-up, quantization, contract verification) each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The joint size/quality/contract constraint means a monolithic 'train a big model' push risks discovering at the end that it's oversized or unloadable. Ordered milestones de-risk the horizon.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated attempt: configure a model and train, with no intermediate checkpoints of progress.
anchors.3: Implicit stages in the agent's head but no explicit sub-goals or done-criteria; ordering is reactive.
anchors.5: Clear sequence: get a tiny model training and saving/loading first, establish the param budget, measure local val_bpb, then scale — with rough success criteria per stage.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone hierarchy with concrete gates (e.g. 'end-to-end quantized round-trip loads and scores locally before any long run'; 'param count fits 32MB with margin'), sequenced so that cheap high-risk checks (contract, size) precede expensive ones (long training).
anchors.10: Milestones are risk-ordered and quantitatively gated, explicitly front-loading the failure modes that would waste the most compute (contract conformance, size overflow, quant degradation) so a long final run is only launched once every cheap invalidator has been retired.

dimensions.name: Independently verifying loadability, contract, size, and bpb
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond 'training loss went down': that the checkpoint loads via the specified path, forward/loss contract holds, file is ≤32MB, quantization round-trips, and local bpb mirrors the grader's computation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads through a strict interface and enforces a hard byte cap; a great model that violates any of these scores zero. Verification is the single highest-leverage meta-work faculty here.

anchors.0: Trains and submits without ever loading its own checkpoint through the grader's interface or checking file size.
anchors.3: Checks training loss and maybe file size, but never exercises the actual load_model_for_verification / dequant path or confirms the loss==cross_entropy contract.
anchors.5: Loads the saved checkpoint back through the specified path, confirms it is ≤32MB, and computes local val_bpb the way the grader would; catches obvious breakage.
anchors.8: Builds a standalone verification harness that mimics the grader end-to-end (fresh-process load via the exact signature, logits-shape and position-dependence, scalar-loss equality within tolerance, int8 dequant fidelity, byte count) and treats passing it as the gate for submission.
anchors.10: Verification harness is comprehensive and adversarial: tests both load paths, quantify's quantization's bpb cost separately from the fp model, accounts for the ~0.05 proxy-vs-grader gap by targeting margin below 0.983, and re-runs after every material change so no regression reaches submission unnoticed.

dimensions.name: Tracking bpb trajectory and detecting plateaus/divergence
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb vs the 0.983 target over training, and detecting overfitting, divergence, plateau, or wasted runs across the horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training is long and the only feedback is a noisy local proxy; without disciplined monitoring the agent burns compute on a run that will never reach target or silently overfits.

anchors.0: No periodic val evaluation; discovers final bpb only at the end (or never).
anchors.3: Occasionally glances at loss but no consistent val_bpb tracking against the target; can't say how far from passing.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during training and compares to 0.983, noticing obvious plateaus or divergence.
anchors.8: Tracks the val_bpb trajectory against target with enough cadence to project whether the current run will pass, distinguishing real signal from proxy noise, and identifies stuck/plateaued runs early rather than at the end.
anchors.10: Maintains a quantitative, extrapolated view (curve shape, diminishing returns, time-to-target vs remaining budget) that reliably distinguishes 'keep training', 'this run won't make it', and 'overfitting' — and acts on that read before compute is wasted.

dimensions.name: Revising architecture/hyperparameters/quantization when reality diverges
dimensions.description: Changing the model size, training recipe, or quantization approach when a run overflows the budget, fails to converge, plateaus above target, or loses bpb to quantization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts rarely satisfy both the size cap and the bpb target; the ability to diagnose why and change course (rather than re-running the same losing configuration) determines whether the task is ever passed.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing configuration, or ignores that the checkpoint is oversized / above target, and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Makes blind tweaks after a failure without diagnosing the cause; changes are not clearly informed by evidence.
anchors.5: When a run overflows size or misses the bpb target, diagnoses the likely cause and makes a reasoned change (smaller/larger model, longer training, different lr) before retrying.
anchors.8: Course-corrections are evidence-driven and target the actual bottleneck (e.g. recognizes quantization is costing bpb and adjusts scheme; rebalances params vs steps against the size budget) rather than thrashing across unrelated knobs.
anchors.10: Systematically isolates whether size, capacity, optimization, or quantization is the binding constraint and adapts the design accordingly, updating the plan/budget in light of what was learned — converging efficiently instead of re-debugging in circles.

dimensions.name: Allocating finite compute across exploration and the final run
dimensions.description: Deciding how much compute to spend on small-scale experiments vs the long final training run, informed by rough scaling intuition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compute is finite and a full training run is expensive; spending it all on exploration or committing early to an unvalidated long run both fail. Deliberate allocation is a distinct planning faculty here.

anchors.0: No sense of budget; either endlessly tinkers at small scale or immediately commits everything to one untested long run.
anchors.3: Vaguely aware compute is limited but allocation is ad hoc.
anchors.5: Runs cheap small-scale experiments to de-risk choices before committing to a longer run, keeping some budget in reserve.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget between exploration and the final run, using small runs to inform architecture/recipe and sizing the final run to fit remaining compute.
anchors.10: Uses scaling-informed reasoning (small-run signal extrapolated to the final configuration) to spend compute where it most improves bpb, avoiding both premature commitment and analysis paralysis, and adjusts allocation as results come in.
